content:
People with good memories might notice it looks somewhat similar to a prototype device called Microsoft Courier, seen way back in 2009.

My headline is obviously tongue-in-cheek: Microsoft’s device never got past the prototype stage and was abandoned within a year. Still, looking back at how similar that prototype is to today’s device in terms of an integrated user interface is quite amazing……

In previous articles, I’ve noted that Apple has shown how to make a foldable smartphone properly, with the clever integration between hardware and software being the key.

One example I gave was dragging part of a photo from one side of the screen to another app, so seeing Microsoft demoing a similar feature in a 2009 concept video is rather funny.

Microsoft later used a similar feature on some Surface products, but ironically it took Apple to finally deliver the level of integration it had originally envisioned. Check out the video below.
